A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIRAGE despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIRAGE restoration results, component and loss ablations, feature analyses, computational measurements, and zero-shot underwater evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds feature-alignment diagnostics and zero-shot evaluations on real under-display-camera images.

M1.justification: The channel partition, attention/convolution/MLP branches, mutual fusion, covariance projections, InfoNCE objective, and reconstruction losses remain unchanged in Algorithms 1, A, B and the corresponding equations. v2 clarifies the projection and non-geodesic formulation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot restoration on TOLED and POLED under-display-camera datasets (Appendix C.6, Table D), extending coverage to real sensor and display-induced degradations. The existing single, combined, weather, and underwater restoration coverage is retained.

E2.justification: DA-RCOT and RamIR are added to both the three- and five-degradation comparisons in Tables 1–2. The new camera comparison includes DiffUIR alongside retained comparators AirNet and PromptIR. Existing comparison methods are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 changes the stated CDD11 training budget from 150 to 170 epochs; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. The added camera evaluation reports LPIPS alongside PSNR and SSIM, while the new diagnostics compare feature similarity under different alignment conditions.

E4.justification: Figures 5–6 add shallow–latent cosine-similarity comparisons and a deraining case study examining alignment collapse under Euclidean contrastive learning. Table D extends distribution-shift testing to real camera degradations. Existing component/loss ablations and channel-redundancy analyses remain, including the previously reported Euclidean contrastive ablation.

E5.justification: Neither PDF supplies repeated-run counts, actual seed values, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's reproducibility statement says random seeds are documented but provides no concrete seed or uncertainty information.

E6.justification: v2 adds comparator scores, alignment measurements, and camera results; Table D places MIRAGE-S ahead of DiffUIR on POLED but behind it on TOLED. PromptIR's Table 2 average changes from 29.15/0.904 to 29.72/0.901 PSNR/SSIM. Section 4.1 also corrects the stated 90%-variance count from 28/192 to 31/192. Existing MIRAGE benchmark and ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical method and loss definitions are retained, including the appendix losses renumbered from Equations 6–7 to A–B. New Appendix B supplies explanatory covariance/SPD background rather than a new theoretical result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an efficient unified restorer combining complementary channel branches with shallow–latent covariance-based contrastive alignment, strong restoration performance, and generalization. The new title and rewritten contribution statements emphasize these existing contributions without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving representation drift, task-dependent feature roles, and Euclidean alignment collapse, and discusses adaptive branch-capacity ratios as future work. It removes v1's specific interpretation of joint versus single-task training. The deblurring limitation and incomplete exploitation of SPD geometry were already disclosed in v1 and remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies PyTorch and single-layer projection MLPs, and supplies a direct repository link stating that code, checkpoints, and visual results are available; v1 promised release through a project page. Most implementation details remain unchanged. v2's reproducibility statement nevertheless retains conflicting future-release wording.

R1.justification: v2 updates the cited literature and adds explicit discussion of contrastive restoration methods, particularly DA-RCOT's residual-space alignment versus MIRAGE's covariance-based alignment. Additional references support RamIR, camera restoration, and recent surveys. The broader positioning as an efficient unified restoration framework remains stable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, substantial method explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around functional decomposition and manifold regularization. References move before the appendices, appendix organization changes, and SPD background, ethics, reproducibility, acknowledgments, and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5–6 and Table D, expands Tables 1–2, and adopts conference typography with revised table and figure placement. Existing architecture diagrams, benchmark displays, and appendix qualitative images are largely retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added baselines, real-camera evaluations, and alignment diagnostics modestly strengthen empirical support and explanation. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: v2 updates PromptIR's Table 2 average but retains the 1.53 dB advantage in Section 5.1, although the revised values imply 0.96 dB. Overall, the additions improve an already extensive evaluation without resolving a major methodological deficiency.
